 Trending Indiana ranked No. 8 in third College Football Playoff rankings reveal 
 Indiana's College Football Playoff projections ahead of third CFP rankings reveal tonight
 The third College Football Playoff rankings will be revealed tonight at 9 p.m. ET on ESPN. Here is where Indiana is projected to be ranked.
 Jared Kelly 0 
 The third College Football Playoff rankings will be revealed tonight at 9 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Indiana could climb in this iteration of the 12-team field. The Hoosiers are 9-1 overall and 6-1 in Big Ten play with two regular season games remaining, and are second in the Big Ten standings.
 According to ESPN's Football Power Index, the Hoosiers have a 85.2 percent chance to make the 12-team CFP field and a 13.7 percent chance to play in the National Championship game. ESPN's analytics also give Indiana a 55.6 percent chance to win the Big Ten and a 5.8 percent chance to win the National Championship.
 IU is favored to win its two remaining games against Washington on the road and Purdue in the regular season finale. The Hoosiers are still on track to return to the Big Ten Championship Game, and they're currently in the driver's seat along with UCLA atop the conference standings.
 So where does Indiana sit in the most recent College Football Playoff projections? Where might the Hoosiers find themselves in tonight's third CFP rankings reveal?
 Here are the latest CFP predictions from notable media outlets and prognosticators.  All relevant links can be accessed by clicking on the bolded font. 
 CBS Sports :  No. 7 Indiana vs. No. 10 BYU (first round; Indiana hosts)
 ESPN: 
 - Mark Schlabach : No. 9 Indiana at No. 8 Tennessee (first round; Tennessee hosts)
 - Kyle Bonagura : No. 8 Indiana vs. No. 9 BYU (first round; Indiana hosts)
 - Heather   Dinich : No. 9 Indiana at No. 8 Tennessee (first round; Tennessee hosts)
 The Athletic: No. 8 Indiana vs. No. 9 Wake Forest (first round; IU hosts)
 Athlon Sports:  No. 3 Indiana vs. No. 6 Miami/No. 11 BYU (first-round bye; Rose Bowl)
 Bleacher Report:  No. 7 Indiana vs. No. 10 BYU (first round; IU hosts)
 Yahoo! Sports: No. 4 Indiana vs. No. 5 Miami/No. 12 Boise State (first-round bye; Rose Bowl)
 College Football News : No. 3 Indiana vs. No. 6 UCLA/No. 11 Wake Forest (first-round bye; Rose Bowl)
 NCAA.com:  No. 8 Indiana vs. No. 9 Tennessee (first round; IU hosts)
 ---
 SEED TOTAL:  No. 3 (2), No. 4 (1), No. 7 (2), No. 8 (3), No. 9 (2)
 OPPONENT TOTAL:  BYU (4), Tennessee (3), Wake Forest (2), Miami (2), UCLA (1), Boise State (1)
 COMMENTS:  The Hoosiers are unanimously projected to be included in the top-12 ahead of tonight's updated CFP rankings, but as has become the case since the CFP rankings were initially revealed, there are wide-ranging opinions on where the Hoosiers will land. It's worth noting that some of these outlets made their projections based on predicted end-of-season results, like Indiana winning out and claiming the Big Ten Championship, while other outlets are only forecasting the current CFP field based on tangible results.
 In the bracket projections which account for end-of-season results, the Hoosiers are being viewed as the Big Ten Championship favorites. If that comes to fruition and IU finishes 12-1 with a conference title in its back pocket, it will be incredibly difficult for the CFP committee not to give Indiana a top-four seed and first-round bye. Of course, the Hoosiers must take care of business on the field for that scenario to play out.
 In projections that only factor in current résumé and body of work, Indiana is somewhere in the 7-9 seed range. That isn't unsurprising ahead of tonight's rankings as no team slotted above Indiana lost this past week. IU could jump a spot or two if the CFP committee deems the win over USC to be more impressive than other wins from teams around Indiana, but no big rankings climb is expected for the Hoosiers just yet.
 The potential opponents for Indiana continue to be a revolving door, and I'd take those predicted matchups with a grain of salt. That said, BYU and Tennessee are the most popular first-round opponents currently, which could set up for a fascinating, non-traditional matchup in the CFP first round. Indiana has played BYU and Tennessee just once all-time, with both games coming in the postseason, but a trip to Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with a CFP Quartefinal spot on the line would be intriguing.
 Based on the top-four seed projections, a return to the Rose Bowl seems likely if Indiana gets a first-round bye. Quarterfinal game locations are based on preference in order of the top-four seeds.
 Tonight's rankings reveal will give us a much clearer idea on how much Indiana's win over USC improved its standing with the CFP committee. It wouldn't be a complete shock either way if Indiana climbs a few spots or stays put at No. 9 based on current projections.
 The third College Football Playoff rankings will be televised tonight at 9 p.m. ET on ESPN.
